_doc: Coefficients of the standing-timber stock of a tile (sim/geography/forest_timber.py). Wood grown and wood stood are both derived from the tile's net primary production, so climate sets them.

entries.unit: dimensionless (stem wood grown per unit of net primary production)
entries.source: Litton, Raich and Ryan 2007, Carbon allocation in forest ecosystems, Global Change Biology 13 (the share of forest NPP going to aboveground woody growth is roughly a quarter to a third), from memory
entries.why: Turns the tile's dry matter production into the stem wood that regrows each year; at temperate production it gives a few tonnes per hectare, in line with the 3-5 cubic metre mean annual increment data/production/30_fuel_stone.json cites for managed forest.

entries.unit: years of stem increment held standing
entries.source: Mature temperate forest holds on the order of one to two hundred tonnes of stem wood per hectare against an increment of a few tonnes (Pan et al. 2011, A large and persistent carbon sink in the world's forests, Science 333), from memory
entries.why: Standing stem wood is the yearly increment times the years the stand has been accumulating it; with the stem share it fixes the tonnes a hectare of untouched forest holds.

entries.unit: kg air-dry wood per kg oven-dry wood
entries.source: Air-dried firewood and roundwood hold about fifteen percent moisture on a dry basis (Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook)
entries.why: Net primary production is in dry matter; wood is cut and traded air-dry.
